package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executable, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: QNodeService is a newly discovered Trojan distributed via Coronavirus-themed phishing campaigns. It is designed to provide remote access to infected systems, enabling attackers to exfiltrate data, execute arbitrary commands, and maintain persistence. The malware is delivered as a malicious file attachment, masquerading as a COVID-19 tax relief document, and is executed by unsuspecting victims. Once executed, it establishes a connection to a command-and-control (C2) server, allowing attackers to control the infected system remotely.

execution_context.trigger: When the victim opens and executes the malicious email attachment
execution_context.file_location: Malicious Windows executable delivered as an email attachment (e.g., disguised as a COVID-19 tax relief document)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The Trojan establishes a connection to a command-and-control (C2) server, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands, upload/download files, and exfiltrate sensitive data. It listens for instructions from the C2 server, executes received commands on the victim's machine, and sends the results or stolen data back to the attacker.
malicious_snippets.code_language: JavaScript (Node.js, as implied by the name QNodeService and analysis of the executable)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the victim executes the malicious attachment, the code initiates an outbound connection to a hardcoded C2 server, receives and executes attacker-supplied commands, exfiltrates files and system information, and transmits results or stolen data back to the attacker, resulting in full remote compromise and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes a persistent outbound connection to an attacker-controlled C2 server, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration without user knowledge. This is a hallmark of backdoor Trojans and remote access malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not open remote command channels, execute arbitrary commands from the internet, or exfiltrate user data without explicit user consent and awareness.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) used in enterprise IT environments may provide similar functionality, but only with user consent, proper authentication, and within a controlled environment. In contrast, QNodeService operates covertly and without authorization.
key_indicators: Outbound connection to hardcoded or attacker-controlled C2 server domains/IPs immediately after execution
Ability to receive and execute arbitrary commands from remote server
File upload/download and data exfiltration functionality
Persistence mechanisms to maintain access after reboot
Execution of Node.js-based code from a Windows executable

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing email with a malicious attachment disguised as a COVID-19 tax relief document.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is enticed to open the attachment.

attack_chain.action: Victim opens and executes the malicious QNodeService executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is loaded into memory and begins execution.

attack_chain.action: QNodeService establishes an outbound connection to the attacker's C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware receives commands from the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Malware receives and executes arbitrary commands, uploads/downloads files, and exfiltrates sensitive data to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote control, can steal data, and further compromise the system.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of unknown Node.js-based Windows executables originating from email attachments
Outbound network connections to hardcoded or known C2 infrastructure immediately after opening suspicious files
Unusual process spawning or command execution initiated by document viewers (e.g., Word, PDF readers) leading to network activity
Persistence mechanisms created by unknown executables (e.g., registry modifications, scheduled tasks)
file_indicators: Unexpected executable attachments with COVID-19 or tax relief themes (e.g., filenames like 'COVID19_TaxRelief.exe')
Files disguised as official documents but containing Node.js or JavaScript code within a Windows executable
Presence of Node.js runtime or related files in temporary or user directories after opening suspicious attachments
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains or IP addresses as listed in threat intelligence feeds
Unusual outbound traffic to unknown domains or IPs immediately after execution of document-themed attachments
Use of uncommon ports or protocols for C2 communication (e.g., non-standard HTTP/S, WebSocket traffic)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of Node.js or JavaScript-based Windows executables originating from email attachments, especially those with COVID-19 or financial relief themes. Detect outbound connections to known or suspicious C2 infrastructure or anomalous domains/IPs following document execution. Alert on processes spawned by document viewers (e.g., Word, PDF readers) that initiate network connections or execute scripts. Look for persistence mechanisms (e.g., registry changes, scheduled tasks) created by unknown executables. Correlate file, process, and network activity to identify multi-stage attack chains.
